report_name: n0n Ransomware Group Adds Backup Destruction to Extortion Tactics

threat_actors.name: n0n
threat_actors.description: A new ransomware group, first observed in September 2026, that employs a triple-extortion model including data encryption, data leakage, and the destruction of victim backups. The group primarily targets the financial services, technology, retail, and education sectors in the United States, using compromised credentials for initial access.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware, data leakage, and threatening to destroy backups.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Used by the n0n group to gain initial access to victim networks, likely leveraging credentials purchased from infostealer malware logs.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Used by n0n operators to gain administrative control over the network, including domain controllers and backup servers, after initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Network Service Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Conducted by n0n attackers to perform network reconnaissance and identify critical assets, data repositories, and backup infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Used by the n0n group to stage and exfiltrate sensitive data to their own infrastructure before deploying the ransomware payload.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The n0n ransomware payload is deployed to encrypt victim files as part of their extortion scheme.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The n0n group specifically targets backup repositories for destruction or encryption to prevent victims from recovering their data.

malware.name: n0n ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the n0n group. It is used in a triple-extortion model that includes encrypting primary data, leaking stolen data, and destroying backups.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete Volume Shadow Copies to inhibit system recovery, as suggested by hunting hints for n0n activity.

tools.name: wbadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete Windows Server Backup catalogs to inhibit system recovery, as suggested by hunting hints for n0n activity.

infrastructure.name: n0n Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A Tor-based dark web site used by the n0n group to list victims and leak stolen data as part of their extortion model.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b9e8a0c-4f1d-4b8a-9c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete all volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware like n0n before encryption.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/new-ransomware-group-n0n-escalates-threats-by-targeting-backups
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
      - '/all'
      - '/quiet'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity, though rare for this specific combination.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the command to delete Volume Shadow Copies, a common precursor to ransomware deployment and a tactic associated with the n0n group.

indicators.name: Wbadmin Backup Catalog Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Wbadmin Backup Catalog Deletion
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-1b0a-9e8f7d6c5b4a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of wbadmin.exe to delete backup catalogs, a technique to inhibit system recovery used by groups like n0n.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/new-ransomware-group-n0n-escalates-threats-by-targeting-backups
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-25
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wbadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'catalog'
      - '-quiet'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity for decommissioning a backup server.
level: high
indicators.description: Detects the command to delete Windows Server Backup catalogs, a tactic used to inhibit system recovery and associated with the n0n group.
